### Pass 199 — Name Use Audit

This pass tests how **name use audit** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners; it does not add a second survivor relationship and memory authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with the material anchors a name card signed in ink, a cup behind a curtain, a photograph with ash at its edge, and a letter sealed with thread. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Name Use Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners; it does not add a second survivor relationship and memory authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with the material anchors a name card signed in ink, a cup behind a curtain, a photograph with ash at its edge, and a letter sealed with thread. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Apology Witness Audit receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 20 high-volume content and story bank — Survivor Relationship And Memory

This bank expands **survivor relationship and memory** through the existing **relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners**. It is authored content and verification scaffolding, not a second authority. Every row carries a stable snake_case ID, schema version, source reference, lifecycle status, localization key, owner, and rollback note. The bank is exercised against **consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval** and uses **a name card signed in ink, a cup behind a curtain, a photograph with ash at its edge, and a letter sealed with thread** as material evidence.

### High-volume field 1 — Audit witness families

The **audit witness families** field covers **audit, confidence, sample, hold, evidence, release, and refusal**. Start with a representative sample, validate it through the current loader and catalog integrity path, then expand by bounded pages. Reject duplicate IDs, unresolved references, unsupported effects, contradictory lifecycle values, and rows with no reachable consumer. Each row states whether it is authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state; a mutable result stays with its canonical owner.

For play, begin with an observable disturbance and offer verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved results. At least one row crosses three existing domains and changes a visible route, relationship boundary, room condition, map confidence, archive entry, or expedition timing. The callback names its publisher, consumer, consequence owner, and source age.

The host supports pagination, filtering, loading, empty, stale, redacted, and error states. Long localization wraps, focus survives refresh, and uncertainty is written rather than encoded by color. Measure first-page latency, allocations, event fan-out, save delta, and safe degradation. A deterministic fixture repeats the same seed and ordered inputs after save and reload. The receipt records source paths, owner evidence, unresolved collisions, migration behavior, rollback, and the stop line if the premise fails.

**Field receipt:** sample IDs; owner API; source references; state ladder; side-quest hook; localization keys; pagination budget; replay fixture; rollback path.

### High-volume field 2 — Review and signal packets

The **review and signal packets** field covers **review, fatigue, seal, visibility, hand signal, acknowledgement, and recovery**. Start with a representative sample, validate it through the current loader and catalog integrity path, then expand by bounded pages. Reject duplicate IDs, unresolved references, unsupported effects, contradictory lifecycle values, and rows with no reachable consumer. These twelve packets turn the new **memory signature and renewal** mechanics into grounded, replayable choices. They remain content-only until the canonical owner, consumer, save route, and deterministic result are proven. ## Wave 20 compact integration and acceptance packet — Survivor Relationship And Memory

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **memory signature and renewal**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 21 — Plan 6 — Survivor Relationship And Memory

Wave 21 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **survivor relationship and memory**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners**. Material anchors include **a folded name card, a cup behind a curtain, a photograph with ash at its edge, and a letter tied with thread**. Observable markers include **consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval**.

### Pass 210 — Name Use Signals

This pass tests how **name use signals** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners; it does not add a second survivor relationship and memory authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with the material anchors a folded name card, a cup behind a curtain, a photograph with ash at its edge, and a letter tied with thread. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Name Use Signals receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

**Name Use Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 22 compact integration and acceptance packet — Survivor Relationship And Memory

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **memory signal and boundary**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Continuation Wave 23 — Plan 6 — Survivor Relationship And Memory

Wave 23 adds a fresh, owner-bound expansion layer for **survivor relationship and memory**. It is a planning scaffold only. The current 30-field structure remains active; these passes add new playable seams, high-volume authoring, story callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners**. Material anchors include **a folded name card, a cup behind a curtain, a photograph with ash at its edge, and a letter tied with thread**. Observable markers include **consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval**.

### Pass 232 — Name Use Charter

This pass tests how **name use charter** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners; it does not add a second survivor relationship and memory authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross consent age, source confidence, contact boundary, memory weight, repair stage, and renewal interval with the material anchors a folded name card, a cup behind a curtain, a photograph with ash at its edge, and a letter tied with thread. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scale, contrast, non-color cues, reduced motion, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, batching, pagination, lazy loading, and safe degradation. Exercise long localization, repeated refresh, missing references, empty catalogs, stale rows, and high-volume records. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, save delta, and first-page latency. The player can cancel, defer, and recover without relying on a single sensory channel or a hidden timeout.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum impact, null semantics, and deletion behavior. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and content correction. Stable ordering cannot depend on wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A stateless projection must reproduce exactly; a durable change must name capture, restore, migration, and rollback.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, data validation, Core or owner contract, event wiring, host route, content sample, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Use focused evidence for the smallest affected region; do not treat a compile result as runtime integration. Record exact files, owner claims, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Documentation volume never promotes a proposal. Rollout begins with a representative sample and expands only after the owner, consumer, persistence, and determinism receipts pass.

**Name Use Charter receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 23 high-volume content and story bank — Survivor Relationship And Memory

### High-volume field 1 — Witness proof families

The **witness proof families** field covers **witness, confidence, sample, hold, evidence, release, and refusal**. ### Pass 243 — Chosen Name Records

This pass tests how **chosen name records** can become a playable, reviewable extension while preserving one authority. It begins with a current-source premise receipt, names the smallest owner seam, and ends with a handoff record.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Verify the current owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, and registration before implementation. The proposal is a bounded extension over relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, and archive owners; it does not add a second survivor relationship and memory authority. Authored data supplies configuration and localization. Mutable progress remains with the current owner, while projections are rebuilt from owner facts. Search current source, catalogs, host routes, and tests for collisions, retired names, and unreachable rows. Record the exact premise receipt and a stop line when the seam cannot be proven.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Define the entry signal, observation, choice, cost, feedback, interruption, refusal, and next action. The player sees name consent, memory provenance, boundary clarity, grief load, repair stage, and renewal window with source and age, then chooses verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. Each command reports validation, resource impact, and recovery. A short session ends with a truthful next action, safe pause, and no duplicate reward. The route must preserve focus and back behavior and must remain useful when the provider is empty, stale, filtered, or partially unavailable.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Specify stable snake_case IDs, schema version, ranges, references, localization keys, migration defaults, and validator diagnostics. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. Missing optional fields receive a documented default; invalid references reject the row without deleting neighboring evidence. Do not encode mutable facts in prose, panel state, or cache keys. Include a representative row, a duplicate-ID fixture, a missing-reference fixture, and a corrected-content migration note before proposing a full bank.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Map pending, offered, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states. Distinguish an offer from an accepted command and an observer event from a durable result. Save at each transition, reload, repeat a command, deliver a duplicate event, and interrupt the host. State who may mutate, which reservation exists, how it releases, and which deterministic fact is visible. A stale or invalid input must converge on one owner result rather than create a shadow state.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Name the existing provider, panel or route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh source, and disposal path. Present name consent, memory provenance, boundary clarity, grief load, repair stage, and renewal window as facts with source, age, uncertainty, and next action; the panel owns no gameplay counter. Empty, loading, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain cause and recovery. Long localization wraps without hiding the command. Closing returns focus to the invoking control. A missing icon, audio cue, or optional row degrades safely while text and navigation remain available.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Connect at least three existing domains and name the publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback for each fact. Cross name consent, memory provenance, boundary clarity, grief load, repair stage, and renewal window with the material anchors a name spoken softly at a doorway, a cup left on a sill, a photograph mended with tape, and a letter folded into a square. A character or place must make a decision under uncertainty that can later be observed in an existing journal, relationship, settlement, power, map, archive, or expedition surface. Subscribers read facts and call the owner; they do not mutate another system. Preserve a visible unknown when sources disagree.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author locations, characters, tasks, rewards, costs, refusal routes, quiet success, costly success, unresolved outcomes, physical clues, and delayed callbacks. The side quest begins with a concrete disturbance rather than a generic fetch request. Give each named person a practical limit and each place a material detail. Branches must alter a reachable owner state or projection. Include repeat policy, retirement condition, localization keys, and a content correction path so revised prose does not erase the player’s evidence.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

**Chosen Name Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Wave 24 compact integration and acceptance packet — Survivor Relationship And Memory

The wave remains a documentation-only proposal over **name consent and memory boundaries**. Before implementation, verify owner, consumer, route, save, replay, accessibility, performance, and rollback. The high-volume bank must pass a representative sample before expansion. Story branches must change a reachable owner state or projection and retain a coherent refusal path. Any missing seam, duplicate authority, unowned mechanic, or contradictory save contract stops the packet and returns it to premise review.

**Five-point handoff:** (1) current-source premise and collision search; (2) one owner and one event/save seam; (3) data, localization, migration, and validator evidence; (4) player route, side-quest callback, replay, accessibility, and performance evidence; (5) exact files, focused verification, limitations, rollback, and next audit.

## Plans 5–8 closeout — Plan 6 integration packet

**Closeout state:** planning-complete, implementation-unclaimed. Plan 6 is ready for a premise audit of one consent-aware memory projection over the current relationship, journal, identity, or time-capsule owner. The first slice reads a durable fact, presents provenance and consent age, and routes view, redact, pause, or renew through the existing owner. It does not add a private-data store, second relationship graph, or shadow memory decay counter.

**Required evidence before implementation:** current relationship/journal command; privacy and consent owner; one reachable host route; one representative memory row; redaction and refusal behavior; old-save and malformed-save behavior; same-seed ordering fixture; focus restoration; long-text and sound-off accessibility; one delayed journal callback; rollback path. Stop if a panel copies private text into local state or if consent is represented only by prose.

**Integration order:** relationship/consent fact → journal or capsule owner → roster/identity projection → narrative callback → UI refresh. The handoff must separate authored voice from durable player memory and must leave unknown identity links unresolved rather than inventing IDs.


## Wave 35 integration closeout receipt — Plan 6: Survivor Relationship and Memory Network

**Closeout status:** documentation-only; READY FOR PREMISE AUDIT. This receipt does not claim implementation.

**Program role:** relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, archive, and social consequence

**Primary owners:** relationship, journal, consent, identity, roster, time-capsule, archive, and social consequence owners

**Required delta:** a consent-aware memory projection over existing relationship or journal facts, with redaction and renewal commands owned by the current systems

**First safe slice:** one remembered promise that can be confirmed, deferred, redacted, or left unresolved and later appears as a journal projection

**Evidence anchors:** a promise card, a worn photograph sleeve, a name token, and a note sealed for later

**Observable signals:** memory source, consent age, trust change, identity confidence, redaction state, and callback date

### Closeout boundary

The plan closes at the design boundary where one current owner can publish a fact, one consumer can display or consume it, one command can be issued through the owner, and one recovery path can return the player to a known state. The plan does not create a second ledger, registry, cache authority, save store, event bus, or presentation-owned counter. A row remains design-only until a current source search proves its consumer.

### Integration contract

The first receipt must identify the owner, public API, data file, save section or stateless proof, host route, focused tests, and rollback. It must exercise source age, stale input, duplicate delivery, interruption, correction, keyboard/controller parity, empty and error states, and one delayed content callback. The same seed and ordered inputs must reproduce the result across save, reload, host reopen, and duplicate event delivery.

### Content and failure gate

The first content slice uses promises, reconciliations, private letters, witness disputes, memorial ties, and renewed consent. It includes discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, choice, quiet success, costly success, refusal, unresolved outcome, delayed callback, repeat policy, and retirement rule. It must stop safely for second relationship graph, private-data leak, memory decay authority, duplicate affinity write, and coercive UI. Prose can describe evidence and uncertainty but cannot create a gameplay fact.

### Handoff

**MUST PRESERVE:** existing authority, engine-free Core, JSON data authority, deterministic ordering, current save ownership, truthful UI, and active path claims.

**MUST ADD:** one premise receipt, one owner-bound slice, one validator-backed sample, one replay or stateless proof, one accessible route, one focused verification result, and one rollback note.

**MUST NOT DO:** duplicate state, revive retired architecture, claim runtime integration from document volume, or widen the catalog before reachability.

**NEXT ACTION:** run the bounded premise audit for the first safe slice and return the evidence to the integrator.
